claim_1.claim: ELISpot analysis of fresh PBMCs from 24 BCG-primed healthy adults showed the antigen-specific IFN-γ response to 85A peptides peaked around 7 days after vaccination (day 7) and remained above baseline for at least 6 months compared to day of vaccination (day 0).

sources.quote: IFN-γ ELISpots to antigen 85A peptide pools were done on fresh PBMC at each time point except day 2

This work shows the majority of the antigen-specific response to MVA85A in BCG-vaccinated individuals is mediated by CD4+ T cells, peaks around 7 days after vaccination and is maintained at a level above baseline for at least 6 months [15,26–29].

comparison.finding: antigen-specific IFN-γ response to 85A peptides peaked at day 7 compared to day 0 baseline and remained above baseline for at least 6 months

claim_2.claim: ELISpot analysis of splenocytes from mice vaccinated with MVA85A showed that adding anti-TLR2 reduced the spread of responses to antigen 85A compared to MVA85A alone or MVA85A plus isotype control, but did not significantly lower the mean response.

sources.quote: The results show a decrease in high responses to antigen 85A. The mean responses are slightly lower than in the control and isotype groups however the main difference seems to be in the spread of the distribution, particularly in the lack of high responses in the group receiving anti-TLR2 antibodies with the vaccine (Figure 5d; all three groups are normally distributed by the D’Agostino and Pearson normality test, F test for differences in variance: p = 0.04 between MVA85A and anti-TLR2, p = 0.02 between anti-TLR2 and isotype groups).

comparison.finding: adding anti-TLR2 reduced the spread of responses to antigen 85A, particularly decreasing high responses, compared with MVA85A alone; mean response was not significantly lower
adding anti-TLR2 reduced the spread of responses to antigen 85A, particularly decreasing high responses, compared with MVA85A plus isotype control; mean response was not significantly lower

claim_3.claim: Transcription profiling by array of unstimulated PBMCs from 24 volunteers showed that 1100 genes were differentially expressed 2 days after vaccination (day 2) compared to day of vaccination (day 0), with enrichment for inflammatory response, positive regulation of the immune response, lysosome and apoptosis genes, and expression had returned almost completely to baseline by day 7.

sources.quote: Comparing two days after vaccination to baseline, 1100 genes were differentially expressed (false discovery rate <0.05).

Analysis of these genes using Gene Set Enrichment Analysis [31–33] (GSEA) and the Database for Annotation, Visualisation and Integrated Discovery [34] (DAVID) showed an enrichment for gene ontology (GO) terms and gene sets relating to an inflammatory response, positive regulation of the immune response, lysosome and apoptosis (Table 1). By day 7, gene expression had returned almost completely to baseline (Figure 1).

comparison.finding: 1100 genes were differentially expressed at day 2 versus day 0, with enrichment for inflammatory response, positive regulation of the immune response, lysosome, and apoptosis genes
By day 7, gene expression had returned almost completely to baseline compared with day 0

claim_4.claim: Transcription profiling by array of unstimulated PBMCs from 24 volunteers showed the greatest gene-expression change 2 days after vaccination (day 2) was in CXCL10 (IP-10), with a fold change of 8.5 compared to day of vaccination (day 0).

sources.quote: The greatest change in gene expression was seen in the interferon-induced chemokine CXCL10 (IP-10) with a fold change of 8.5 on day 2 compared to day 0.

comparison.finding: CXCL10 (IP-10) showed the greatest gene-expression change on day 2 versus day 0, with a fold change of 8.5.

claim_5.claim: Transcription profiling by array of PBMCs stimulated in vitro from day-of-vaccination samples showed that about 50% of the genes upregulated in vivo at day 2 were also differentially expressed in vitro, and these genes were enriched for phagocytosis, chemotaxis and inflammatory-response terms compared to controls.

sources.quote: Of the 1100 genes differentially expressed on day 2 in the volunteers, 50% were also differentially expressed in the cells stimulated in vitro. These genes were enriched for GO terms including phagocytosis, chemotaxis and the inflammatory response.

claim_6.claim: Transcription profiling by array of PBMCs stimulated in vitro showed that infection with either MVA85A or MVAwt led to differential expression of around 5000 genes compared to control, more than 3000 genes were modulated by both MVAs, and 176 genes differed between MVA85A and MVAwt.

sources.quote: Infection with either MVA85A or MVAwt leads to differential expression of around 5000 genes compared to the control; of these, over 3000 were modulated by both MVAs. 176 genes show significant differential expression when PBMC were stimulated with MVA85A compared to MVAwt.

claim_7.claim: Transcription profiling by array of PBMCs from 24 volunteers showed that 176 genes were differentially expressed 2 days after vaccination (day 2) between high and low responders, and genes contributing to regulation of T-cell activation and co-stimulation were more highly expressed in low responders compared to high responders.

sources.quote: Two days after vaccination, 176 genes were differentially expressed between high and low responders.
The genes contributing to the enrichment of these clusters, which are more highly expressed in low responders, are shown in table 2.

comparison.finding: 176 genes were differentially expressed at day 2 between high and low responders; genes contributing to regulation of T-cell activation and co-stimulation were more highly expressed in low responders than in high responders

claim_8.claim: Transcription profiling by array of PBMCs from 24 volunteers showed that on day of vaccination (day 0), TLR1, TICAM2 and CD14 were more highly expressed in high responders than low responders and together could classify individuals as high or low responders with 79% cross-validation accuracy; adding CTLA4 and IL2RA measured 2 days after vaccination (day 2) increased cross-validation accuracy to 88%.

sources.quote: The three genes retained were: TLR1, CD14 and TICAM2.

Using linear discriminant analysis (LDA), the mRNA levels of TLR1, TICAM2 and CD14 on day of vaccination could classify individuals as high or low responders with a cross-validation accuracy of 80%. Doing the same LDA analysis on the original 24 samples, using microarray values for the expression levels of the same three genes, the cross validation accuracy was 79% (Figure 3b).

Although no discriminatory gene set was found based on gene expression 2 days after vaccination, adding CTLA4 and IL2RA (CD25) to the LDA model developed with the three innate sensor genes refined the model and increased its cross validation accuracy to 88% (Figure 3c, d).

comparison.finding: On day 0, TLR1, TICAM2 and CD14 were more highly expressed in high responders than low responders and together classified individuals as high or low responders with 79% cross-validation accuracy.
On day 2, adding CTLA4 and IL2RA to the day 0 model refined classification of high versus low responders and increased cross-validation accuracy to 88%.

claim_9.claim: Transcription profiling by array of PBMCs from 24 volunteers showed that TLR1 mRNA on day of vaccination (day 0) correlated with ELISpot AUC immunogenicity compared across individuals.

sources.quote: The levels of TLR1 mRNA in both trials correlated with AUC (Figure 4a; p < 0.05, Spearman’s r = 0.70, p<0.01, Spearman’s r=0.55 respectively).

claim_10.claim: Flow Cytometry analysis of PBMCs from the same volunteers showed that the CD4+ CD25+ Foxp3+ Treg population increased between day of vaccination (day 0) and 7 days after vaccination (day 7) in low responders but not high responders compared to baseline.

sources.quote: In high responders, the number of Tregs (as a percentage of CD4+ cells) remained constant pre- and post vaccination, however in low responders it increased between day 0 and day 7 (Figure 2a, p = 0.009).

comparison.finding: CD4+ CD25+ Foxp3+ Treg population differed by responder status at day 0 baseline
At day 7, the CD4+ CD25+ Foxp3+ Treg population was increased in low responders but not high responders compared to baseline

claim_11.claim: Flow Cytometry analysis of PBMCs from 24 volunteers showed that surface TLR1 expression on all live cells on day of vaccination (day 0) correlated with immunogenicity measured by IFN-γ ELISpot AUC across individuals.

sources.quote: There was a correlation between the level of TLR1 expression on day of vaccination and AUC, although the relationship was weaker at the protein level compared to the mRNA (Figure 4b,c; p<0.05, Spearman’s r=0.45).

claim_12.claim: Q-PCR analysis of PBMCs from 10 samples in the validation trial showed that expression of TLR1, TICAM2 and CD14 on day of vaccination (day 0) classified high and low responders, and TLR1 expression correlated with ELISpot AUC immunogenicity across individuals.

sources.quote: We measured the expression of the nine genes by qPCR and again classified the volunteers as high or low responders based on the median AUC value for their ELISpot responses
The three genes retained were: TLR1, CD14 and TICAM2.
The levels of TLR1 mRNA in both trials correlated with AUC (Figure 4a; p < 0.05, Spearman’s r = 0.70, p<0.01, Spearman’s r=0.55 respectively).

comparison.finding: expression of TLR1, TICAM2 and CD14 on day 0 classified high and low responders

claim_13.claim: Q-PCR analysis of PBMCs stimulated in vitro showed that neutralizing antibodies to TLR1, TLR2 or TLR6 decreased CXCL2 mRNA production in response to MVA85A compared to MVA85A with no antibody or isotype control.

sources.quote: neutralising antibodies to TLRs 1, 2 or 6 or HMGB1 decrease CXCL2 production during in vitro stimulation with MVA85A.

groups.cohort: MVA85A with no antibody or isotype control
MVA85A with neutralizing antibody to TLR1
MVA85A with neutralizing antibody to TLR2
MVA85A with neutralizing antibody to TLR6

comparison.finding: neutralizing antibody to TLR1 decreased CXCL2 mRNA production in response to MVA85A compared to MVA85A with no antibody or isotype control
neutralizing antibody to TLR2 decreased CXCL2 mRNA production in response to MVA85A compared to MVA85A with no antibody or isotype control
neutralizing antibody to TLR6 decreased CXCL2 mRNA production in response to MVA85A compared to MVA85A with no antibody or isotype control

claim_14.claim: Q-PCR analysis of PBMCs stimulated in vitro showed that anti-HMGB1 reduced CXCL2 mRNA production in response to MVA85A compared to MVA stimulation alone.

sources.quote: Furthermore, anti-HMGB1 antibodies also reduce the production of CXCL2 in cells stimulated with MVA85A (Figure 5b, c).

claim_15.claim: Western blot analysis of cell supernatants showed that HMGB1 was released into the supernatant after MVA stimulation, being detectable by 4 and 6 hours, compared to unstimulated cells.

sources.quote: HMGB1 is detectable by western blot in the supernatant of infected cells 4 and 6 hours post infection but not in the supernatant of uninfected cells after 6 hours.
